The grievance of the petitioner as articulated in the present petition is apropos the communication dated 30.08.2024 (hereinafter 'impugned communication') issued by the Deputy Director (LM) NDZ addressed to the Executive Engineer (SPD)-1, DDA Office Complex, Nelson Mandel Marg, Vasant Kunj, New Delhi -110070.
5.

sentences.text: A perusal of the said impugned communication shows that the DDA has intimated the Executive Engineer (SPD)-1 about the decision taken by the higher authorities to carry out TSS (Technical Sight Survey) of 356 Bigha 9 Biswa DDA land acquired vide Award no. 07/98-99 dated 22.06.1999.

It is further alleged that physical possession of the said land was handed over to DDA by LAC/ L&B Deptt., GNCTD.
6.

The case of the petitioner is that the aforesaid land was sought to be acquired by the respondent GNCTD by issuing a notification dated 01.06.1995 under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894.
Subsequently, Section 6 notification was also issued on 24.06.1997.
The aforesaid acquisition proceedings culminated into an Award 07/98-99 dated 22.06.1999.
The petitioner's land is stated to be included in the said Award.

7. The petitioner challenged the 1996 acquisition proceedings, as well as, the Award before this Court by way of petition W.P. (C) 3732/1999 titled as Shri Mansukh Bhai Kothari and Ors. v. Union of India and Ors.

entities.text: Shri Mansukh Bhai Kothari and Ors. v. Union of India and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said petition was, however, dismissed by this Court vide judgment dated 16.05.2008.

The relevant part of the said judgment reads thus:
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 27/06/2025 at 23:28:51 "3.

A fresh notification under Sections 4 and 17 was then issued by the competent authority for acquisition of different parcels of land including an area of 369 bighas and 1 biswa situated in village Rangpuri.

This notification issued on 27th June, 1996 was followed by a declaration under Section 6 of the Act on 24 th June, 1997 for the land sought to be acquired including the land owned by the petitioners.
Notices under Section 9 and 10 of the Act were issued nearly 2 years later to the interested persons including the petitioners asking them to file their claims and objections.

Upon consideration of these claims and objections,
the Collector, Land Acquisition made and published award No.7/1998- 99/SW on 22nd June, 1999.
Dissatisfied with the award, the petitioners have filed the present writ petitions challenging the validity of the acquisition proceedings on several grounds to which we shall presently advert.

8. Feeling aggrieved, the petitioner assailed the said judgment of this Court by filing SLP (C)
20953/2008 titled Mansukh Bhai Kothari and Ors. v. Union of India and Ors. upon leave being granted.

sentences.text: 9. Mr. Rajiv Nayar, the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner invites attention of the Court to the order dated 01.09.2008 passed in SLP 20953/2008 whereby the Hon'ble Supreme Court had ordered to maintain the status quo regarding the possession of the subject property.
10. Subsequently, the SLP was converted into Civil Appeal No. 4294/2011 and the same was disposed of vide judgment dated 12.01.2015
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 27/06/2025 at 23:28:51 whereby the acquisition proceedings in respect of the subject land were quashed.

The relevant part of the judgment reads thus:
".....The right conferred to the landholders/owners of the acquired land under Section 24(2) of the Act is the statutory right and, therefore, the said right cannot be taken away by an Ordinance by inserting proviso to the abovesaid sub-section without giving retrospective effect to the same.

Taking into consideration the fact that we have allowed similar matters in C.A. No. 4284/2011 titled M/s. Magnum Promoters P. Ltd. Vs. Union of India & Ors., vide order dated 27.11.2014 and in other appeals also by following the earlier decisions of this Court with regard to taking physical possession of the acquired land by the Land Acquisition Collector, which are extensively referred in the above judgment, promulgation of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014 was made on 31.12.2014, which is prospective in nature and, therefore, it cannot be applied to their cases.

entities.text: Magnum Promoters P. Ltd. Vs. Union of India & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: For the foregoing reasons, the interlocutory applications are allowed and consequently, the appeals are also allowed by quashing the acquisition proceedings in relation to the applicants/appellants."
(emphasis supplied)
11. He submits that since the acquisition proceedings had been quashed, therefore, the award passed in respect of the subject land does not survive.

Therefore, the DDA has no authority to issue the impugned letter seeking to carry out the Technical Sight Survey and assert possession over the land of the petitioner i.e. Farm no. 19, Shivji Marg, Rangpuri, New Delhi admeasuring 2.5 acres and Ms Chaturbhuj Finance Limited vs Deputy Director Land Management New ...

He submits that the apprehension of the petitioners is that the respondent/DDA might try to demolish the construction raised over the subject land take possession of the same.
Mr. Nayar submits the said apprehension stems from the fact that the DDA has already carried out demolition in the adjoining land which was also the subject matter of the same award.
In support of his submission, Mr. Nayar has drawn attention of the Court to the photographs annexed to the present petition.

13. In view of the above, issue notice to the respondent, by all permissible modes, returnable on 01.09.2025.
14.
Let counter-affidavit be filed within a period of four weeks.
Rejoinder thereto, if any, be filed within a period of two weeks thereafter.

15. In the meanwhile, having regard to the submissions made by Mr. Rajiv Nayar, more particularly to the fact that the acquisition proceedings which culminated into an Award 07/98-99 dated 22.06.1999 were subsequently quashed and set aside by the Hon'ble Supreme Court vide its judgment dated 12.01.2015 passed in the above noted Civil Appeal, this Court is of the view that the petitioners have made out a prima facie case for grant of interim relief.
Accordingly, the respondent is directed not to act pursuant to the impugned communication dated 30.08.2024 and maintain status quo as regards the possession of the subject land, till the next date.
16. Dasti under the Signatures of the Court Master.
VIKAS MAHAJAN, J MAY 29, 2025 N.S. ASWAL
